rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should test a key design choice: multimodal (combining RNA and image data) with multiprofile settings. This isolates the impact of multimodal integration and multiprofile handling, which are critical for cellular profiling. Testing this configuration clarifies whether these complex settings provide performance benefits over simpler alternatives, balancing exploration of high-impact decisions with foundational understanding.

Existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200 + resnet50, avgpool + weighted) achieves 0.677 validation accuracy. This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder) while keeping other components identical. It isolates the impact of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision, and could reveal whether ViT improves performance. This addresses uncertainty about encoder effectiveness while building on the existing multimodal/multiprofile foundation.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder (config_009) outperforms resnet50 (config_001). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 (config_009) to pca_n2000 while keeping the image encoder, aggregation (avgpool), and fusion (weighted) the same isolates the impact of RNA representation. This clarifies whether RNA encoder choice is critical, balancing exploration of key design decisions with exploitation of the promising image encoder.

Existing evidence shows that using ImageNet ViT-L as the image encoder (config_009) outperforms ResNet50. This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation (a key design choice) further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It exploits the strong evidence for ImageNet ViT-L while exploring a critical component of multimodal fusion.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (as in config_015) yield high accuracy. This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder (scvi_n200 → scgpt) while keeping image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), aggregation (transformer), and fusion (weighted) consistent. This isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, and explores whether a more advanced encoder (scgpt) improves performance without changing other factors.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l (config_009) and transformer aggregation (config_015) improves performance. This experiment tests combining these two successful changes (vit_l image encoder + transformer aggregation) to determine if their combined effect further enhances accuracy. It isolates the impact of these key design choices while building on prior promising directions.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and imagenet_vit_l image encoder contribute to high performance (config_041: 0.725). This experiment tests whether replacing scvi_n200 RNA encoder with pca_n2000 (while keeping other components unchanged) affects performance. It isolates the RNA encoder's impact, a critical design choice, and could clarify if pca_n2000 is a viable alternative. This balances exploitation of current strong components with exploration of RNA encoder variations.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_041) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether using pca_n2000 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (vs. scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l) impacts performance, isolating the effect of encoder choices. It balances exploration of RNA/image encoder trade-offs while keeping aggregation/fusion consistent with top-performing configurations.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_041) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests the effect of changing fusion to concat while using transformer aggregation, isolating its impact. It also compares the resnet50 image encoder against the previously successful imagenet_vit_l, helping determine if the image encoder choice is critical. This balances exploration of fusion methods with minimal changes to the proven effective setup.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (as in config_041) yield high performance. This experiment tests whether switching to concat fusion while keeping other components (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation) the same clarifies if fusion method is a critical factor. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy without altering other high-performing components, balancing exploration of key design choices with exploitation of existing strong results.
